basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Holds the intended definition of a product, not a built item or its measured state.
Owns a controlled technical package and its revision baseline, while CAD files and drawings remain external masters.
Traces requirements to design elements, unlike a requirement record that only states what is needed.
Feeds the engineering BOM and variant definitions but does not itself list component occurrences or selections.

may: Resolve the released baseline and list its package members.
Trace which design elements realize a given requirement revision.
Inspect geometry, units and PMI through approved tooling and report findings.
Draft change requests and deviation reports for review.
mustNot: Treat a valid design record as proof of fitness, certification or export permission.
Modify a released revision instead of creating a controlled change.
Send technical data across a border or to third parties without export and contract checks.
Infer requirement satisfaction from the presence of a trace link.
Drive manufacturing or physical actuation directly from the design record.
requiresHuman: Approving deviations, waivers and engineering changes.
Authorizing release of technical data outside the organization.

considerations: Design errors propagate to every item built, so safety-relevant assumptions must stay visible and reviewed.
Technical packages can carry export-controlled or dual-use information.
Design rationale and authorship should be preserved so accountability is clear after incidents.
affectedParties: End users and the public exposed to the product
Manufacturers and maintainers who build from the definition

items: A design is identified by part or document number, revision and release state in a PDM or PLM system.
Physical parts reference it through drawing and revision marks.
Confused with a CAD file, a drawing sheet, a requirement, the BOM and the physical part.
Building to an unreleased or superseded revision.
Unit or tolerance errors lost in data exchange.
Unauthorized disclosure of controlled technical data.
Unverified design assumptions reaching safety-critical use.
ISO 10303-242 (STEP AP242) for managed model-based 3D engineering.
ISO 10303-239 (PLCS) for product life cycle support.
ISO 1101 and ASME Y14.5 for geometric tolerancing.
Nominal dimensions in millimetres with tolerances and the datum reference frame.
Design mass in kilograms, stated as calculated from geometry and material density.
Material specification by referenced standard designation.
Surface finish, such as roughness Ra in micrometres.
Rated loads, pressures or temperatures in SI units, with the design condition stated.
Each value marked as nominal design intent, not measured.
